headline: This law reauthorizes a major foreign intelligence surveillance authority until 2023 and adds new limits, reporting duties, and oversight rules.
what_it_does: The law extends Section 702 of FISA, which lets the government collect communications of non-U.S. persons located outside the United States, until December 31, 2023. It requires the Justice Department to set querying rules that must keep a record of each query term used to search for information about U.S. persons, and it limits how the FBI can review query results in some criminal cases without a court order. It also adds new reporting, oversight, whistle-blower protections for contractors, and a higher penalty for taking classified documents without authorization.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. persons whose communications may be swept into foreign intelligence collection
who_it_affects.how: Searches of collected data using their identifying information must be recorded and are subject to new querying rules and limits on use in criminal cases.

who_it_affects.group: FBI agents and Justice Department attorneys
who_it_affects.how: They must follow new querying procedures, keep records of U.S. person query terms, and get a court order in certain criminal investigations before reviewing some query results.
Contractor employees of the intelligence community and the FBI now have whistle-blower protections.

who_it_affects.group: People who take or keep classified documents without authorization
who_it_affects.how: The maximum prison penalty for this offense increased from one year to five years.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law on January 19, 2018, with the surveillance authority extended through December 31, 2023.
